interpreter_classes.bash: reads incrementally: rewrite mid-run can splice new bytes into the running interpreter. Loud outcome: syntax error (the demonstrated incident — the LUCKY case). Quiet outcome: half-old/half-new logic executing (mixed thresholds, mixed counters) reporting wrong verdicts as fact. Exposure scales with runtime.
interpreter_classes.python: parses whole file at startup: immune mid-run. Residual: rewrite landing between open and parse (~ms at exec start) -> SyntaxError at startup, loud. Lowest exposure class.

method: runtime measured live at HEAD (single runs; fleet/beads-dependent paths vary — lane-status observed 1.1s here, slower under fleet waits); edit-frequency = git log --oneline -- count per file (session-lifetime); exec-frequency from wiring (tick first-action / every-commit hooks / suite runs / by-hand); consequence = loud-vs-quiet splice + criticality

ranking.consequence: SILENT splice of derived counters/verdicts reported as lane fact; loud variant blocks tick reporting
ranking.exec: tick first-action + ad-hoc by all panes (highest non-hook frequency)
ranking.why: most-edited + most-run + bash-incremental + verdict output. Runtime understates: fleet/beads waits make slow runs the norm under load, widening the window exactly when edits cluster.

ranking.consequence: syntax error mid-suite (demonstrated) or mixed old/new stage semantics; suite verdict unreliable either way
ranking.exec: full-suite runs before commits and verifications
ranking.why: longest runner; the demonstrated incident file. Lower edit rate than #1 keeps it second.

ranking.consequence: fail-OPEN (dropped deletion sails through = data-loss class) or fail-closed lane-wide commit block. Splice window is ms but execution is constant and criticality is maximal.
ranking.why: frequency x criticality beats window size. The one file where a quiet splice destroys evidence rather than misreporting it.

ranking.consequence: mixed old/new stage semantics inside a suite run
ranking.why: slowest stage, edited 3x already (glob, messages, exclusions) — churn concentrates here.

ranking.consequence: parse-at-startup immunity; residual ms startup race only
ranking.file: python scripts (audit-score-lineage, verify-other-reasons, selftest-other-reasons, selftest-score-lineage is bash—see note)
ranking.why: NOTE: selftest-score-lineage.sh and selftest-lane-status-integrity.sh are BASH (4.3s and ~1s, 4/3 edits) — mid-pack exposure, not immune; only the .sh-suffixed python files are. Suffix lies; interpreter decides.

ranking.consequence: message-format fail-open/closed; reviewed content, lower criticality than pre-commit

ranking.why: 70 edited once and fires live — low exposure, high value.

recommendation.lock: NO — new failure surface with no owner in a 3-pane tree; a stale lock blocks the lane worse than a splice (splices are loud more often than not, locks fail silently by design).
recommendation.structural: Runtime IS exposure for bash: keep stages short (second argument for the ~30s gates.sh budget), and prefer python (parse-at-start immunity) for long-running new instruments. Suffix discipline: stop naming python files .sh.
recommendation.discipline: Before editing rank 1-3, broadcast hold-runs via hub send to all ('editing X, hold runs 60s'). No lock state, no owner, uses the existing coordination surface. Edits to the rest need no ceremony.
recommendation.git_note: `git checkout -- <script>` mid-run is the same splice class as editing — the hazard is write-during-exec, not the editor.
